case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Best bet: South Haven pier, rated 1 (below average).** Go there if you're fishing the pier this week.
- **Second: St. Joseph pier, rated 1.** Fish here if South Haven is too far or the wind is wrong.
- **Grand Haven pier, rated 1.** Pier fishing has been slow.
- **Muskegon pier, rated 0 (slow).** Skip it for salmon this week.
- Set up for the water, not the pier: boats have been doing best 55 to 110 feet down in 110 to 210 feet of water, and that is where the pier crowd should look for fish if they move.

## Why
- The only pier-specific salmon reports in the last four weeks were rated slow, at Grand Haven and Muskegon (Grand Haven, 2026-09-14; Muskegon, 2022-09-07), so no port has a strong pier rating right now.
- I'd expect South Haven to edge ahead because the Sept 7 South Haven boat report was good, and that week's buoy showed more upwelling wind there than at the other ports.
- I'd expect Muskegon to rank last because its Sept 7 report found no salmon at the breakwalls, and it had the least upwelling of the four.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (newest is 2022-09-14, six days old):**
- Grand Haven, 2022-09-14: "The pier action was slow for salmon." Boats did well 55 to 110 feet down in 120 to 210 feet of water, quality 3, on green, yellow and orange spoons and green and white flies.
- Muskegon, 2022-09-07: "No salmon were reported from the breakwalls." Boats were fair 45 to 90 feet down in 60 to 120 feet of water. No Muskegon pier report appeared for Sept 14.
- St. Joseph, 2022-09-14: "There were a couple of boats fishing the pier heads and caught a couple of coho and Chinook." No pier-angler report appeared.
- South Haven, 2022-09-07: Boats had "pretty good fishing," quality 3, 110 to 120 feet of water, with spoons, rotators and flies. The best water was around 40 feet. No South Haven pier report appeared in the last four weeks.

**Past seasons (similar water temperature, within 21 days of today; history, not current):**
- The same pattern shows up in the matched weeks: boats do best in deeper water, and the pier reports are slow. I found no past week with a strong pier rating at these four ports in this window.

**Conditions now:**
- The conditions tool returned a backtest summary for the week before Sept 20, not live data. I did not have a live buoy reading, a live pierhead model, or a live wind forecast.
- That summary put South Haven's upwelling wind at 16 hours in 7 days (14 in the last 3), the most of the four ports. Grand Haven had 14, Muskegon 20 (10 in the last 3), and St. Joseph 9.
- Surface water was about 70 to 71 F across the ports. This is in the 52 to 58 F range salmon prefer only near the cold layer, so the fish are likely deeper than the surface.

## Caveats
- The newest pier-specific report is six days old, and the season changes quickly in September. Treat these ratings as a guide.
- The South Haven and St. Joseph pier ratings are my estimates. No pier-angler salmon report was published for either port in the last four weeks, so the rating is partly an inference from boat reports and wind.
- The temperature and wind figures are not live. Check the buoy and the wind forecast before you go.
- Holland was not included because it has only one report.

- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph, Sept 7 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32bbcf0
- Aug 24 bulletin (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3298204
